edges.effect_quant: Prospective high-versus-low comparisons are close to null, while broader observational and dose-response analyses often show a small upward association that may be heavily confounded by smoking.
edges.mechanism: Coffee metabolites are excreted through the urinary tract, so a bladder signal is at least biologically discussable, but there is no strong mechanistic case that rivals tobacco-related urothelial carcinogenesis. The most plausible explanation for the harmful-looking observational association is residual confounding by smoking and correlated behaviors.
edges.summary: This edge is better read as unresolved than as genuinely harmful. The updated prospective-only meta-analysis found no clear association, whereas broader observational and dose-response syntheses tended to show a small increase in bladder-cancer risk, leaving smoking confounding as the central interpretation problem.
edges.caveats: Smoking is such a dominant bladder-cancer determinant that even good adjustment may not fully remove its influence. Case-control studies also make recall bias and exposure misclassification more likely than in cleaner prospective cohorts.
